title: Collinear motions in constant curvature spaces, and coplanar motions in $\mathbb{R^4}$
summary: A collinear motion of an $n$-body problem is one in which the $n$-bodies always lie along some, possibly moving, geodesic during their evolution. We prove that every collinear motion of $n\geq 3$ bodies in a constant non-zero curvature space is necessarily contained in some fixed constant curvature space of dimension at most three. For natural systems admitting energy and angular momentum integrals, we further show that every such motion is necessarily a relative equilibrium: evolving under uniform rotation while maintaining constant mutual distances.
